AI LEARNING FEATURE USABILITY STUDY 2026

Modeling Misclick Changes Across the Roadmap

Estimating design impact across iterations to assess launch readiness, spark design improvements, and reinforce confidence in the product’s winning qualities.

The product demonstrated strong task effectiveness but weak path efficiency. Benchmarked design comparisons show meaningful reductions.

The Pilot launch experience’s central model estimates meaningful usability improvement, with a visible uncertainty range. Product leadership determines whether the available evidence, technical readiness, and remaining uncertainty are acceptable for launch.*

The roadmap’s central model estimates a 58.2% reduction, leaving 627 misclicks. The model range leaves 571 to 712 misclicks, but the remaining count is not a backlog of known defects. It is the modeled remainder after the Pilot recommendations.

Why the model does not assume 100%: The recommendations are intended to remove the systematic friction identified in the study, but not every recorded misclick can be attributed to a specific design issue. The model learned from the three tested design comparisons. It estimates that an improved design has about 31.4 misclicks for every 100 misclicks in the older design. Put simply, the middle estimate is 68.6% fewer misclicks. The model’s likely range is 53.3% to 78.9% fewer. We apply that range to recommendations without a direct comparison. This is a conservative evidence boundary, not the design team’s performance target.

The remaining misclicks may include:

  • Residual friction that still existed in the better tested variants
  • Misclicks caused by multiple issues within the same task
  • User exploration, especially when learning an unfamiliar AI workflow
  • Individual variation in how participants interpreted the task
  • Issues not isolated by the study’s task-level data
  • New or different friction that could appear when all changes are integrated

Evidence-based next step: Re-test the integrated Pilot with the same tasks and metrics, locate where residual misclicks concentrate, then prioritize the next design cycle by frequency, severity, and impact on critical-task success and recovery.

Tested comparisons quantify observed differences. For recommendations without a direct comparison benchmark, the model applies the pooled 68.6% reduction estimated across the three benchmarked design comparisons (incidence-rate ratio 0.314; 95% CI 0.211 to 0.467), with a model range of 53.3% to 78.9% fewer. The individual benchmarked reductions were 57.6%, 38.0%, and 81.4%. The pooled estimate is model-based and does not equal their simple average. Modeled values are directional and are not measured post-change performance. Reliably determining realized savings and launch readiness requires testing the integrated updated product.

* Industry standards define what to evaluate, but do not prescribe a universal acceptable misclick count or percentage. Targets should be set by the product team based on task, risk, and a repeatable benchmark.

This study: 91.3% overall mission completion across 230 of 252 attempts, with individual flows ranging from 86% to 100%. Among 219 successful attempts with retained misclick metrics, 19.6% were direct successes with zero misclicks and 80.4% were indirect successes with one or more misclicks. Because the study was unmoderated and the prototype accepted only the correct CTA, indirect success means participants independently recovered after an incorrect interaction.

EVIDENCE BASE

Tested evidenceDirect design comparisons quantify observed differences.
Estimated evidenceThink of the model as looking at three before-and-after pictures. It counts each person’s misclicks, notices that some people click more than others, and learns one middle-sized improvement. The model is a negative-binomial generalized estimating equation, which is made for count data with many small values and a few big values, and it accounts for the same people appearing in more than one comparison. The middle estimate is 68.6% fewer misclicks, and the model range is 53.3% to 78.9% fewer. We use the middle number for the solid progress bar and the range for the lighter uncertainty band. This is a projection, not a promise. What does “negative-binomial” mean? Read a friendly 3-minute explanation ↗
Technical nameNegative-binomial generalized estimating equation with participant clustering, comparison controls, and counterbalance-group control. The pooled improved-design incidence-rate ratio is 0.314 (95% confidence interval 0.211 to 0.467).
Benchmarked reductions57.6%, 38.0%, and 81.4%.
InterpretationModeled values are directional, not measured post-change performance.
ValidationTest the integrated Pilot implementation to determine realized savings and launch readiness.

Study details and source

Industry reference Approximately 78% average task completion across 1,189 tasks in 115 studies.

This study 91.3% overall mission completion across 230 of 252 attempts, with individual flows ranging from 86% to 100%.

Path efficiency Among 219 successful attempts with retained misclick metrics, 19.6% were direct successes with zero misclicks. The remaining 80.4% were indirect successes with one or more misclicks. Because the study was unmoderated and the prototype accepted only the correct CTA, participants recovered independently after an incorrect interaction.

Interpretation: Repeated tasks can provide more information when the analysis keeps attempts grouped within each participant. Treating all 252 attempts as unrelated observations would overstate certainty. For a formal comparison with the 78% external reference, use participant-clustered inference and treat the reference as contextual rather than as a matched control condition.
Study 91.3% | Reference 78% | +13.3 percentage points

No pre-study target

Study details and source

What was established before the study No direct-success or misclick target was defined before testing. No universal misclick threshold is available; appropriate targets depend on task risk, error consequence, opportunities for error, and recoverability.

This study The tested prototype established a baseline of 19.6% direct, zero-misclick success among successful attempts with retained metrics: 43 of 219. The remaining 80.4% included at least one misclick.

Interpretation The 19.6% result is a descriptive baseline, not a pass or fail against a predetermined standard. It should be used to compare the integrated Pilot with the tested prototype.

Post-study design direction Increase direct success and reduce consequential or difficult-to-recover misclicks. Critical and exploratory workflows should be evaluated separately because the consequence and acceptable recovery burden differ.

Next step Define task-specific Pilot targets before the next validation study, document those targets in the study plan, and evaluate improvement against this baseline.

Use 19.6% as the baseline for evaluating the integrated Pilot
